grammar.title: Asking Prices: How much is / How much are
grammar.explain_en: Use 'How much is' for one thing (singular) and 'How much are' for more than one thing (plural).
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng 'How much is' đối với món đồ số ít và 'How much are' đối với các món đồ số nhiều.
examples: How much is this shirt? It is 100,000 dong.
How much are these socks? They are 40,000 dong.
How much is the blue wallet? It is 80,000 dong.

grammar.title: Comparatives: Cheaper than & More expensive than
grammar.explain_en: Add '-er' for short adjectives (cheap -> cheaper). Use 'more' before long adjectives (more expensive).
grammar.explain_vi: Thêm đuôi '-er' với tính từ ngắn (cheap -> cheaper). Dùng 'more' phía trước tính từ dài (more expensive).
examples: The pencil is cheaper than the pen.
The bicycle is more expensive than the ball.
Bread is cheaper than birthday cake.
grammar.right: ✅ This doll is more expensive than the toy car.
grammar.wrong: ❌ This doll is expensiver than the toy car.

grammar.title: Past Simple: Irregular Verbs Buy & Sell
grammar.explain_en: The past simple form of 'buy' is 'bought'. The past simple form of 'sell' is 'sold'.
grammar.explain_vi: Dạng quá khứ của 'buy' là 'bought' (đã mua). Dạng quá khứ của 'sell' là 'sold' (đã bán).
examples: Mai bought a new wallet yesterday.
The shopkeeper sold all the storybooks.
We bought fresh fruit at the market.

grammar.title: Future Intentions: Will & Be going to
grammar.explain_en: Use 'will' or 'am/is/are going to' to talk about shopping plans in the future.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng 'will' hoặc 'am/is/are going to' để nói về kế hoạch mua sắm trong tương lai.
examples: I will buy a new notebook tomorrow.
She is going to buy groceries this afternoon.
They will pay by cash.
grammar.right: ✅ I will go to the bakery later.
grammar.wrong: ❌ I will going to the bakery later.

readings.title: AT THE SUPERMARKET
readings.text: Today is Saturday. Nam and his mother are at the big supermarket near their house. The supermarket is clean and brightly lit. Nam pushes a green shopping cart while his mother picks fresh yellow bananas and red apples. Nam wants to buy a new notebook for school. He looks at the shelf. The blue notebook is 15,000 dong. It is cheaper than the pink notebook. His mother buys the blue notebook for him. They go to the friendly cashier. Mother pays in cash and gets 10,000 dong change. Nam puts everything into a reusable shopping bag. He feels happy.

readings.title: MAI'S NEW BACKPACK
readings.text: Mai needed a new backpack for Grade 4 because her old backpack was small and torn. Yesterday afternoon, Mai and her father walked to the central shopping mall. First, they visited a store with many colourful bags. Mai saw a beautiful purple backpack with star patterns. She checked the price tag on the side. The purple backpack was 250,000 dong. Next to it was a red backpack for 180,000 dong. The red backpack was cheaper, but Mai liked the purple one very much because purple is her favorite color. Her father asked the cashier, 'Can I pay by cash?' The cashier smiled and said, 'Yes, of course!' Her father handed three 100,000 dong notes and received a paper receipt along with 50,000 dong in change. Mai thanked her father cheerfully.

readings.title: THE SCHOOL FLEA MARKET
readings.text:
Last Sunday, Primary School No. 1 organized a charity flea market in the main school yard. Students brought old toys, handmade crafts, storybooks, and delicious homemade snacks to sell to each other. Minh and his group set up a small table named 'Happy Books & Toys'. Minh brought five comic books and three small robot toys that he did not play with anymore. His friend Linh baked tasty chocolate cupcakes. They marked clear prices on every item with small yellow paper tags.

At nine o'clock, many customers visited their table. Ben, a classmate, walked over and asked, 'How much is this comic book?' Minh replied, 'It is 10,000 dong. It is very cheap and interesting!' Ben decided to buy two comic books. Later, Mia came and bought two cupcakes for 20,000 dong. By eleven o'clock, Minh and Linh had sold all their items. They collected a total of 180,000 dong in cash in their blue pencil box. They were very proud because all the money collected from the market will go to buy winter clothes for poor children in rural areas. Shopping and selling at the market was not only fun, but it also taught them how to manage money and share love with community.

We bought one kilogram of apples for 40,000 dong and two bottles of milk for 30,000 dong. Next, we walked to the school section because I needed a new pencil case. life_skill.title: BE A SMART SHOPPER & RESPECT MONEY
life_skill.intro: Money is earned through hard work. Being a smart shopper means buying what you need and spending wisely!
life_skill.intro_vi: Tiền bạc được làm ra từ sự lao động vất vả. Trở thành người tiêu dùng thông minh nghĩa là mua những gì mình cần và chi tiêu hợp lý!
can_do: Make a shopping list before going to the store.
Compare prices before choosing an item.
Buy things I really need before buying things I want.
Keep money safely in a wallet or piggy bank.
Check the change carefully after paying cash.
Keep receipts to check expenses at home.
Use reusable shopping bags to protect the environment.
Turn off lights and save water to help family save money.
Take care of my school supplies so I do not waste money.
Share old usable books at flea markets for charity.
Say thank you politely to cashiers and shopkeepers.
Never demand expensive toys from parents.
life_skill.value_question: What can you do to spend money wisely and help your family save?
life_skill.image_prompt: A thoughtful Vietnamese student writing a neat shopping list on paper before going grocery shopping with family.

fun_facts.en: Did you know? In ancient times, people did not use paper money; they traded cows, salt, and seashells for goods!
fun_facts.vi: Thời cổ đại, con người không dùng tiền giấy; họ trao đổi bò, muối và vỏ sò để lấy hàng hóa!

fun_facts.en: Did you know? Some of the first coins in the world were made in Lydia (in today's Turkey) about 2,600 years ago!
fun_facts.vi: Em có biết? Một trong những đồng xu đầu tiên trên thế giới được làm ở xứ Lydia (nay thuộc Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ) khoảng 2.600 năm trước!

fun_facts.en: Did you know? US dollar notes are not made from wood paper. They are made from cotton and linen!
fun_facts.vi: Em có biết? Tiền đô la Mỹ không làm từ giấy gỗ mà làm từ sợi bông và sợi lanh!

fun_facts.en: Did you know? Vietnamese Polymer banknotes are water-resistant and much harder to tear than plain paper notes!
fun_facts.vi: Tờ tiền Polymer Việt Nam có khả năng chống nước và khó rách hơn nhiều so với tiền giấy thường!

fun_facts.en: Did you know? The concept of price tags on store items was invented over 140 years ago in the United States!
fun_facts.vi: Ý tưởng dán nhãn giá lên hàng hóa trong cửa hàng được phát minh cách đây hơn 140 năm tại Mỹ!

classroom_game.name: ROXY CLASSROOM FLEA MARKET
classroom_game.players: Whole class in small groups of 4
steps_en: Step 1: Each group sets up a mini shop table with classroom items (pens, rulers, books).
Step 2: Write paper price tags (from 5,000 to 50,000 dong) for each item.
Step 3: Two students act as cashiers and two students act as buyers with play money.
Step 4: Buyers ask 'How much is this?' and compare prices before buying.
Step 5: Switch roles after 5 minutes and see which group manages money best!
steps_vi: Bước 1: Mỗi nhóm bày một bàn cửa hàng nhỏ với đồ dùng học tập (bút, thước, sách).
Bước 2: Viết nhãn giá bằng giấy (từ 5.000 đến 50.000 đồng) cho từng món đồ.
Bước 3: Hai bạn đóng vai thu ngân, hai bạn đóng vai người mua với tiền đồ chơi.
Bước 4: Người mua hỏi 'How much is this?' và so sánh giá trước khi mua.
Bước 5: Đổi vai sau 5 phút và xem nhóm nào quản lý tiền tốt nhất!
